question: Give a full row for the Wallowa Matterhorn standard route from Ice Lake; should the Matterhorn get its own peak area; is the Sacajawea-Matterhorn traverse worth adding?
answer: The standard route is the Ice Lake climbers trail: from the Wallowa Lake trailhead to Ice Lake, then a worn path over shale bands and a rounded marble dome to the summit (about 3.6 mi and 1,980 ft beyond Ice Lake; the Ice Lake hike itself is 15.4 mi RT, 3,380 ft, high point 7,900). Oregon Hikers tags it a scramble/off-trail; logs call it class 2 with no technical moves. Continuing north over an intermediate dome to Sacajawea needs a couple of basic climbing moves with exposure; trip reports (snippets, not fetched) call the full ridge class 3 with some avoidable class 4 and gendarmes that can be bypassed in west-side scree. Summit 9,826 ft (Oregon Hikers) vs 9,834 ft lidar (Peakbagger, most recent, use this); coordinate 45.22781,-117.29932 (PB) / 45.22770,-117.29910 (OH). Our area or_ice_lake_peaks holds Matterhorn West Face Chimney/Wall, Razzberry Mt (a different peak) and Exegesis, so it is a multi-peak grouping.
recommendation: ADD route 'East Ridge from Ice Lake' (scrambling, class 2) and 'Sacajawea-Matterhorn Ridge Traverse' (scrambling, class 3). Create a new PEAK area 'Matterhorn' under parent or_wallowa_mountains at 45.22781,-117.29932, elev 9834 ft, and move the two West Face rows onto it (leave Razzberry and Exegesis on or_ice_lake_peaks). Run catalog_find_area('Matterhorn','Oregon') first to avoid the duplicate trigger. Trailhead pin: Wallowa Lake Trailhead 45.26704,-117.212834 is confirmed by a fetched page (the start, ~6 mi from Ice Lake).

routeRow.name: East Ridge from Ice Lake
routeRow.overview: The usual way up the Wallowas' marble peak. A climbers path leaves the Ice Lake basin, crosses wet meadow and bands of shale, then climbs a rounded dome of pale marble to the top. Mountain goats are common, and most parties camp at Ice Lake.
routeRow.approach: Hike the East Fork Wallowa River trail from Wallowa Lake to Ice Lake. From the lake follow the climbers path up the peak, roughly 3.6 mi round trip and 2,000 ft of gain.
routeRow.descent_text: Retrace the climbers path to Ice Lake; the dome and shale bands are easy to reverse in daylight.

traverseRow.name: Sacajawea-Matterhorn Ridge Traverse
traverseRow.overview: A ridge link between the two highest summits of the range, usually done from an Ice Lake camp. An intermediate dome and a few gendarmes lie between; a couple of exposed class 4 moves can be avoided by dropping into scree on the west side.
traverseRow.approach: Climb the Matterhorn from Ice Lake, then follow the crest north. Return by the same ridge or via the scree and creek on the Sacajawea side.
